builder.language: python3 standard library only; no network, no subprocess, no JVM tool
builder.reason: The two faults are single count fields in an otherwise reviewed input; the handler variant additionally needs the variable-length handler record rebuilt so the count fault stays the only malformed field.

originalInput.note: Every register word (v0, v1 with registers_size 2), the one type reference and the handler address 2 (inside the 6-unit method) are in range, so both variants start from a reviewed valid input. The method declares outs_size 0 and contains no invoke, so no external binding is required.
originalInput.codeUnitMeaning: unit0 const/4 v0,5 (normal path); unit1 return v0; unit2 move-exception v1 (handler entry at addr 2); unit3 const/16 v1,7; unit4 is the literal word 7 of the 21s const/16, not a separate instruction; unit5 return v1. The handler therefore returns the separately defined int 7 instead of the caught reference, so f()I is type-correct on both paths.
originalInput.handlerOffMeaning: try_item.handler_off is measured from the start of encoded_catch_handler_list, so it is 1 to skip the list's own ULEB count at byte 0; the single encoded_catch_handler therefore begins at f_handler_list_off+1 and its record ends exactly at class_data_off with no padding gap.

variants.changedBytesNote: the four patched bytes at 0x184..0x187 plus the recomputed 4-byte header checksum and 20-byte signature at 0x08..0x1f

variants.rebuiltDependents: The handler record grows 1 -> 5 bytes at offset 413, so every later byte shifts by 4: class_data_off moves 416 -> 420, map_off 432 -> 436 and file_size 556 -> 560 before the count fault is applied.
variants.changedBytesNote: A positional byte comparison reports 88 differing offsets, which is the 4-byte shift artifact, not 88 independent edits: the only authored edits are the 1-byte ULEB count replaced by the 5-byte SLEB at 413 and the recomputed header checksum and signature.

certificationObligations: Each variant runs independently; neither is merged into one any-error invocation.

The fault certificate proves the field overrun from the checked minimum byte count: insns_size*2 = 4294967294 bytes against 164 remaining bytes, and handler |size|*2 >= 4294967294 bytes against 142 remaining bytes after the SLEB.
The handler variant certifies that the SLEB32 5th byte payload is 0x07, inside the allowed 0x00..0x07 range, so the encoding is legal while the count is not.
The certificate records the original field value, the patch offset and the rebuilt hash for each variant, and confirms no second malformed field was added.
An independent decoder confirms both variants keep the same declaration, refs, version and register words as the original; the only malformed field is the patched count.
gaps: The independent dexlib2 projection and the Engine classification are not executable here; B03 owns the projection and its hashes.
Misclassification as BudgetExceeded versus Malformed is an Engine behavior this worktree cannot observe.
pathBase: case-root: every repository source path is relative to tests/e2e/sources/<case>/, and every generated artifact path is relative to the repository root under .cache/e2e/.
measurementPolicy: Asset sizes and hashes are produced by preparation from actual bytes under the ignored execution workspace; no author cache or hand-maintained measurement file is a prerequisite.
